newsitem.title: LEBANON: BLC star of Beirut Stock Exchange for second week.
newsitem.headline: BLC star of Beirut Stock Exchange for second week.

text.p: Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce was the star performer in the week ended on Friday on the Beirut Stock Exchange for a second week running.
Solidere shares fell on the week after a 10-for-one stock split which took effect on Monday.

BLC shares, continuing a strong performance since they listed on the exchange 12 days ago, rose 4.25 percent to $12.25 from $11.75 last Friday. Weekly turnover was 49,000 shares against last week's 17,000 shares.
Also 17,500 BLC shares changed hands in block trades inside the bourse hall during the week for a value of $211,563.
"BLC is looking good," one dealer told Reuters.
"We see the trend is upwards but gradual for the shares. There is a lot of demand but the market makers don't want it to go up too fast so they are executing the orders little by little," he said.

BLC is the first commercial bank to list on the Beirut exchange since the market reopened a year ago. With the exception of one trading day this week when BLC was inactive, the shares have steadily risen from $11.25 on December 30 when they began trading.
Solidere A shares fell 1.8 percent to $11 from last Friday's $11.2 ($112 before the split) and B shares fell 2.2 percent to $11.25 from last week's $11.5 ($115 before split).
Weekly turnover in Solidere shares fell sharply to 102,180 shares from last week's 386,340 and value was $1,145,910.625 from $4,344,747.
Also traded on the BSE during the week were 6,280 shares of Ciments Libanais at $1.1562 and 100 shares of piping maker Eternit at $1.75.
There was no trade in the two other listed firms: Ciments Blancs and Uniceramic.
The LISPI stock index fell 0.21 percent on the week to 81.59 and the BLOM stock index fell 1.58 percent to 933.11.
